title: Verb + -ing (enjoy doing / stop doing etc.)
subtitle: enjoy doing / stop doing
summary: Use the -ing form after verbs like enjoy, mind, suggest, stop, finish, avoid and after give up, put off, go on and keep (on).

lesson.heading: enjoy / mind / suggest + -ing
lesson.text: After **enjoy, mind** and **suggest**, we use **-ing** (not to ...). Some more verbs that are followed by -ing: **stop, finish, recommend, consider, admit, deny, avoid, risk, imagine, fancy**.

examples.text: I **enjoy reading**.
Would you **mind closing** the door?
Chris **suggested going** to the cinema.
Suddenly everybody **stopped talking**. There was silence.
I'll do the shopping when I've **finished cleaning** the flat.
He tried to **avoid answering** my question.
I don't **fancy going** out this evening.
Have you ever **considered going** to live in another country?
They said they were innocent. They **denied doing** anything wrong.
When I'm on holiday, I enjoy **not having** to get up early.

lesson.heading: give up / put off / go on / keep on + -ing
lesson.text: We also use -ing after **give up** (= stop), **put off** (= delay until later), **go on** or **carry on** (= continue) and **keep** or **keep on** (= do something continuously or repeatedly).

examples.text: I've **given up buying** newspapers. I don't read them any more.
You shouldn't **put off telling** him what happened. You need to tell him now.
Katherine doesn't want to retire. She wants to **go on working**.
You **keep interrupting** when I'm talking.

lesson.heading: Verb + somebody + -ing
lesson.text: With some verbs you can use the structure **verb + somebody + -ing**.

examples.text: You can't **stop people doing** what they want.
I can't **imagine George riding** a motorbike.
Did she really say that? I don't **remember her saying** that.
Sorry to **keep you waiting** so long.

lesson.heading: having done
lesson.text: When you talk about finished actions, you can say **having done / having stolen** etc. But it is not necessary to use having (done) - the simple -ing form is also fine.

examples.text: They admitted **having stolen** the money.
examples.note: or They admitted stealing the money.

examples.text: I now regret **saying** that.
examples.note: or I now regret having said that.

lesson.heading: Other structures with admit, deny, suggest, recommend
lesson.text: After **admit, deny, suggest** and **recommend** you can also use a *that* clause instead of -ing.

examples.text: They **denied (that) they had done** anything wrong.
Chris **suggested (that) we go** to the cinema.
I **recommend (that) you travel** by train.

lesson.text: Learn these as a group: enjoy, mind, suggest, stop, finish, avoid, fancy, consider, admit, deny, risk, imagine - all take -ing, never to ...

exercises.explanation: After enjoy we use -ing: enjoy listening (not enjoy to listen).

exercises.prompt: 'Do you want to play tennis?' 'No, not really.' He didn't fancy ___.
exercises.explanation: fancy is followed by -ing: didn't fancy playing tennis.

exercises.prompt: 'Let's go for a walk.' 'Good idea!' She suggested ___.
exercises.explanation: suggest is followed by -ing: suggested going (not suggested to go).

exercises.prompt: 'You caused the accident.' 'No, I didn't.' He denied ___.
exercises.explanation: deny is followed by -ing: denied causing the accident.

exercises.prompt: Match each verb with its meaning.

pairs.right: say that you did not do something

exercises.prompt: I'm trying to concentrate. Please stop ___ so much noise!
exercises.explanation: stop + -ing: stop making so much noise.

exercises.prompt: We need to change our routine. We can't go on ___ like this.
exercises.explanation: go on (= continue) + -ing: go on living like this.

exercises.prompt: I've put off ___ this bill so many times. I really must do it today.
exercises.explanation: put off (= delay) is followed by -ing: put off paying.

exercises.prompt: It's OK if you want to drive my car. Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: I don't mind you driving it.
exercises.explanation: verb + somebody + -ing: I don't mind you driving it.

exercises.prompt: Would you mind not ___ me all the time? Let me speak!
exercises.explanation: The negative form after mind is not + -ing: mind not interrupting.

exercises.prompt: I'll be as quick as I can. Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: I don't want to keep you waiting.

exercises.statement: They admitted having stolen the money.
exercises.explanation: Correct. For a finished action you can say having stolen (or simply admitted stealing the money).
